findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Inspector observed raw shell eggs stored directly above grapefruit in the walk-in cooler. The PIC was informed and the eggs were relocated. Ensure proper storage order is followed to prevent cross contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: Inspector observed cardboard boxes of food stored directly on the floor of the walk-in freezer. The PIC was informed that items must be stored at least 6 inches off the ground. The PIC acquired plastic pallets and moved items off the floor during the inspection. This violations is now corrected on site.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: Observed no sanitizing solution available for use during food service and preparation. Solution was made during inspection, and tested at 200 ppm Cl-.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment: One employee does not have food handler training. Ensure all employees have food handler training as soon as possible.  410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
Wet wiping cloth observed on the drainboard of the 3 compartment sink. Keep wiping cloths submerged in sanitizer when not in use. CORRECTED- Cloth returned to sanitizer bucket.
3-304.14: (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114  (P) Chlorine sanitizing rinse at dish machine 10ppm and 120°F. A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution. Options: 25ppm to 49ppm when the temperature is at least 120°F and the pH is 10 or less; or (2) 50ppm to 99ppm when the temperature is at least 100°F and the pH is 10 or less, or when the temperature is at least 75°F and the pH is 8 or less; or (3) 100ppm when the temperature is at least 55°F and the pH is 10 or less. Reference 4-501.114. Test machine daily before use. 
Technician came over with chlorine and adjusted the machine accordingly. Now 50ppm Cl.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: Observed tomato and egg on the salad bar at between 44F and 54F.  Ice was added to the bus tubs. The food shall either be held at proper temperature or with time as a public health control. 750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above) The food will be discarded after this lunch.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment: The sanitizer concentration in the dish machine is 0ppm of sanitizer. The machine will not be used to sanitizer until proper sanitizer can be added to the machine. The machine can be used to washed and rinsed but sanitize in the 3 part sink at 50ppm of chlorine sanitizer for one minute of contact time. 750-830 All chemical sanitizers in a dish machine must meet the requirements of 21 CFR 178.1010 to ensure all items are properly sanitized.  Rinse water shall not be less than 75F. Provide proper sanitizer concentration.

findings.title: Rooms clean, lockers provided and used, clean
findings.comment: Observed a phone and a water bottle on the prep table in the kitchen. Do not set personal items onto prep surfaces. The phone and water bottle were immediately removed. 750-1280 Adequate area must be provided for the storage of employee belongings segregated from the food preparation and food storage area to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all employee belongings.

findings.title: Dishwashing facilities designed, constructed, operated (1. wash 2. rinse 3. sanitize)
findings.comment: Observed the dish wsahing process to be conducted as wash, sanitize, rinse.  Employees were coached and procedure adjusted. 750-820a For manual washing, rinsing and sanitizing of utensils and equipment, a sink with no fewer then three compartments shall be provided and used in the order wash, rinse and sanitize.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: Observed the water tray in the ice machine to be soiled. 750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use and any time they may have become contaminated.  Properly clean and sanitize this area.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: The following non food areas are soiled with dust and dirt: 1) area under salad bar behind doors 2) fan cover in the glass front beverage cooler. 750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
Observed the make up air covers overs on the hood vents to be soiled with dust and dirt. 750-1220 Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings. Clean and maintain free of accumulated soil.
Observed a large hole in the wall under the hand sink in the dish room. Also the collar at the mop sink is missing on one side and not sealed on the other. The mop sink is not sealed to the wall at the base. 750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and  rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings. Repair these area.

findings.title: Rooms clean, lockers provided and used, clean
findings.comment: Observed that there is a key on the prep table. Also observed some personal food in the walk in cooler and upright 2 door. 750-1280 Adequate area must be provided and used for the storage of employee belongings segregated from the food preparation and food storage area to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all employee belongings. All personal food must be kept separate from the food for service to the students. Foods were moved to a bus tub and placed on the floor in the walk in cooler.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - General surfaces of food service line were observed being wiped with a damp cloth containing only water. Use of sanitizer solution for wiping general surfaces was discussed.

Maintain a solution at proper concentration for wiping surfaces, and change the solution as needed when solution and/or wiping cloths become heavily soiled.
Bleach solution should be at 100-200ppm and quat solutions should be at 200-400ppm. (do not mix)

findings.title: Single service articles not re-used
findings.citation_text:
750.600 - Plastic cottage cheese and yogurt containers were observed being reused for storing sprinkles in the dry storage room. Obtain and use proper re-usable food containers for storage of sprinkles and other foods.

Re-use of single-service articles is prohibited. Do not re-use single service items. Anything that came with a food product already in it is considered single service (i.e. yogurt containers, bread bags, etc.), and items such as aluminum roaster pans, aluminum pie pans, etc. should not be used more than once.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment:
7 50.510 - Worker was observed washing hands without proper technique. Handles of the manual faucet and paper towel dispenser were touched without use of a barrier upon completing handwashing process. Proper technique was discussed with Kitchen Manager and the worker.

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time they may have been contaminated, before putting on gloves/between glove changes, and prior to working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles. Have paper towels ready to dry hands prior to washing hands. To avoid re-contamination of freshly washed hands use the paper towels as a barrier to turn off the faucet and touch the handle of the paper towel dispenser if more towels are needed.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - Commercially processed, individual packets of light ranch dressing were observed in direct contact with cleaned/portioned servings of fresh vegetables in the 2 door cooler. Employee doing prep was advised to change practice and place ranch packets in a separate container for persons  to grab as they go through the lunch line. The outer surface of the ranch packets is not considered a clean surface.

Foods shall be properly stored and protected from potential contamination at all times.
Employee stated she would remove the packets from the ranch portioned vegetables in the cooler and re-wash the vegetables before serving.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment:
750.830g - (R) Quat sanitizer test kit has not been purchased since the last inspection. The quat sanitizer used for wiping down tables in the cafeteria requires a different test strip than the dish machine, which uses a chlorine based sanitizer. Obtain and use quat test strips for checking the concentration of the product (200-400ppm). 
(see general comments)

A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of each chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solutions in parts per million.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text:
750.1220 - (R) Mouse droppings were observed in the dry storage area along walls/in corners beneath shelving. General cleaning and monitoring for signs of rodent activity were discussed with Kitchen Manager. (see general comments)

Clean the floor in the dry storage room and check the areas of concern every day to monitor for rodent activity.
.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.151 - Several ready to eat, potentially hazardous foods were not date marked in the walkin cooler and included deli meats, sliced tomatoes, diced ham and American cheese. Manager stated foods were opened/prepared as of 1/12. Manager was allowed to date and keep the foods in question for use.

Refrigerated ready to eat, potentially hazardous food shall be clearly marked with the date and used or discarded within 7 days. Day one begins as soon as prep occurs and/or the original packaging is opened. If portions of a product are frozen, then the clock stops on the 7 day time frame. However, the amount of time available to use that product once pulled from the freezer and thawed for use is no longer 7 days. Amount of time left to use the product after thawing is dependent upon when the product was frozen within the 7 day time frame. Keep track of dates when products are opened, frozen, and thawed in order to accurately monitor the 7 day time frame for use.
Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment:
750.830g - A new quat sanitizer is being used to wipe down tables in the cafeteria. Staff do not have quat test strips. Obtain and use quat test strips for checking the concentration of the product (200-400ppm).  (see general comments)

A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of each chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solutions in parts per million.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text:
750.1220 - Mouse droppings were observed in the dry storage area one wall/in corners. Custodian was shown areas where droppings were noted. Mice have not been observed or caught recently (droppings appeared to be old). Custodian planned to place glue traps in addition to snap traps.

Clean the floor in the dry storage room and check the areas of concern every day to monitor for rodent activity.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.citation_text:
750.1060 - Dish machine has a leak somewhere underneath (possibly at the end of the motor). A plastic container was observed underneath to catch dripping water; water and small pieces of debris were observed in the container. The container was emptied at the mopsink during the inspection. The leak doesn't happen all the time, and a work order was placed ~2 weeks ago. Staff were advised to keep the container clean and empty it daily/as needed until proper repairs have been made (water in container could serve as a water source for pests).
All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair the dish machine in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text:
750.1200 - Floor in walkin cooler has several spots where paint has begun to chip away exposing rusty floor underneath. Repaint the floor.
All floors must be in good repair, constructed to facilitate easy cleaning, and maintained clean.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.citation_text: 750.690 - Metal shelves in walkin cooler have heavy rust accumulation. It is time to clean and paint the shelves or replace them. Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750.800e - Counters under pizza ovens and cheese sauce dispenser were soiled with dust and debris. Clean under the aforementioned equipment. Non-food contact surfaces should be cleaned daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text: 750.1200 & 1220 - A) (R) Floor to wall juncture in dry storage room has gaps, and a small hole was observed at one corner. Areas were shown to kitchen manager. Floor to wall juncture in dry storage room needs to be sealed to eliminate gaps where debris may accumulate and/or serve as a hiding place for pests. Junctures between walls and floors shall be coved and sealed. B) Floors were observed to be soiled in the following areas: 1. old mouse droppings along walls in the dish area, behind ice machine/chemical storage shelves, and behind stove, 2. debris along walls in dry storage room, 3. dead roach under 3 part sink, and 4. puddling condensation, moisture, & debris along juncture where walkin cooler & freezer meet the floor. Clean the floor in the aforementioned areas.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750.800e - The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled: A) bottom underneath dish machine (dust); B) Legs, brackets, and general surfaces on the underside of dish counter/tray return (dust); & C) side of fryer (grease/food debris). Clean all non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.citation_text: 750.880 - Plastic forks, knives, and spoons were not all facing one direction in organizer; handles and food surfaces were intermixed. Single-service articles shall be stored, handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user. Store all utensils facing one direction so only the handle is touched when retrieving utensils. **When stocking plastic utensils wash hands and put on a pair of gloves due to plastic-ware being shipped in bulk packaging with food contact surfaces and handles intermixed**

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text: 750.1200 & 1220 - A) Floor to wall juncture in dry storage has gaps in various spots. Inspector showed Custodian areas of concern, and it was noted the gaps would be sealed with caulk by custodial staff. B) Floor in dish area along wall and in corners below tray return window had some debris accumulation. Clean the floor along the wall/in the corners at the tray return window in the kitchen. Junctures between walls and floors shall be coved and sealed, and floors shall be kept clean.

findings.title: Foods properly cooked and/or reheated
findings.citation_text: 750.210 - Portioned green beans leftover from Friday were reheating in the warmer. Beans were at 110F and were in the warmer for ~45 minutes according to kitchen manager. Beans were placed in a pot on the stove to finish rapidly reheating to 165F prior to portioning and placing back in the warmer for hot holding. PHF shall be reheated rapidly to 165F/higher throughout the product. Properly reheat food using equipment intended for reheating. Warmers (hot boxes) are meant to hold foods at 135F/above after they have already been properly cooked or reheated to appropriate temperatures using equipment such as stoves, microwave, and ovens. Do not use the warmer for cooking/reheating purposes.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text: 750.530 - Employee was observed chewing gum while working in the kitchen/doing food prep. Employee discarded gun in the trash during the inspection. Employees shall consume food, including candy and gum, only in designated dining areas. Do not eat candy or chew gum while doing food prep or working in the kitchen to avoid potential contamination of food, equipment, utensils, and other surfaces.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750.800e - An old mouse dropping was observed on the top of the small bulk food storage lid in the dry storage room. Kitchen manager stated mice have not  been an issue lately. No other droppings were noted elsewhere. Thoroughly clean the lid of the small bulk food bin. Also clean the vertical brackets of all metal shelving where dust/debris accumulation is present. Clean non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of food, debris, and dust.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text: 750.1200 & 1220 - A) Old glue trap with dead bugs/debris was observed in dry storage room behind bottled water storage. Also, a dead bug was observed under the 3 part sink. Clean the floors throughout daily and switch out glue traps as they accumulate debris and insects. B) Dry storage room - 1) floor tiles at the corner by electrical panel were loose/damaged. Wood base below the electrical box had gaps/damaged areas that need to be properly sealed. 2) Gaps were observed along the floor to wall juncture at various spots in the dry storage room (i.e. corners behind spice and towel storage, etc.). Repair/properly seal the aforementioned areas in the dry storage room. The junctures between walls and floors shall be coved and sealed.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: Observed a gap in the behind the wall and the 3 compartment sink on the North wall. Section 750.690 Seal the gap.

findings.comment:
Observed a gap in behind the 3 compartment sink in the kitchen.
